statement_bytes:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$, be a bounded smooth domain, and let $\gamma_1,\gamma_2\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega,\mathbb R)$ be strictly positive. If their full physical conductivity Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps agree on all boundary data, then every inward boundary-normal derivative agrees:
$$\partial_{x_n}^k\gamma_1|_{\partial\Omega} =\partial_{x_n}^k\gamma_2|_{\partial\Omega} \qquad(k=0,1,2,\ldots),$$
where $x_n=\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)$ in a boundary normal collar.

0.1 We first make explicit the full physical DN map and the identity on a possibly disconnected $\Omega$. The compact smooth manifold $\overline\Omega$ has finitely many connected components $M_a=\overline\Omega_a$, $1\le a\le J$: connected coordinate neighborhoods give an open cover, and a finite subcover meets every component. Each $M_a$ has nonempty boundary; otherwise its same-dimensional inclusion in $\mathbb R^n$ would make it both open and compact, impossible for a nonempty subset of $\mathbb R^n$. Thus the connected-domain suppliers [F1] and [F2] apply on every $M_a$. Fixed finite atlases identify $H^1(\Omega)=\bigoplus_aH^1(\Omega_a)$ and $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)=\bigoplus_aH^{1/2}(\partial\Omega_a)$, with the corresponding finite sum for the boundary dual. The full physical map is $\Lambda_\gamma=\bigoplus_a\Lambda_{\gamma|_{M_a}}$: solve separately on each component, and its weak boundary pairing is the sum of the component weak pairings. This is exactly the global physical flux pairing, not an additional assumption on the conductivities or data. Equality of the global maps implies equality of the component maps by inputs and tests supported on one component. Applying [F2] on each component and summing gives the global Alessandrini identity used below. The quasimode supplier [F3], Proof 5.1, already constructs the exact solutions componentwise. Boundary normal collars and derivatives are componentwise as well. Consequently all later localization and normal-jet steps apply without a connectedness restriction.
